title: Launch Approval Runbook — SIEM, RBACv2 & Auditlog Evidence
content:
Purpose:
This runbook defines the pre-launch security gating and sign-off requirements for Redwood product releases that touch authentication, authorization (RBAC v2), auditing, or SIEM integrations. It combines checklist steps, required evidence artifacts, automated collection points, and an exceptions approval workflow. Intended audience: product release owner, engineering lead, security reviewer, SRE, and Compliance.
body:
Executive summary:
- Aim: ensure every launch that modifies access controls, log emission, or telemetry exports is validated against RBAC v2 policies, audit-log schema expectations, and SIEM export policies before production rollout.
- Outcomes: clear pass/fail gate, packaged evidence bundle for audits, and a documented exception path if a requirement cannot be met before release.

Launch classification decision:
- Low-risk: UI text-only, non-auth changes — follow lightweight QA checklist.
- Medium-risk: changes to roles, permission lists, or logging levels — use this runbook.
- High-risk: new integrations with third-party SIEM, changes to auth flow, or wide-scope RBAC refactors — require SIRT review and extended hold.

Preconditions (owner responsibilities):
1) Attach the proposed change PR and architecture diagram to the release ticket.
2) Notify security@redwood 72 hours before code freeze for medium/high-risk launches.
3) Confirm the feature toggle exists and is controllable per-environment.

Checklist: (each item must be Yes/No and linked artifact attached)
- RBAC v2 policy review:
  - All affected roles enumerated and documented (link: ROLE-MAP).
  - Least-privilege justification provided for any elevated permissions.
  - Automated policy unit tests added to CI and passing.
- Audit log schema validation:
  - Events introduced by the change mapped to the audit schema (event_type, actor_id, target_id, timestamp, old/new).
  - Log sizes/field cardinality reviewed for cardinality explosion risks.
  - Sample log lines (10-20) included in the evidence bundle.
- SIEM export & PII handling:
  - Export transformation config reviewed to ensure PII redaction for fields marked sensitive.
  - Mapping to SIEM field names and types documented.
  - Export throughput test performed in staging to validate batching and backpressure behavior.
- Evidence automation artifacts:
  - CI job artifact link showing policy unit test results.
  - Audit log synthetic replay job run (staging) with attachments.
  - Export sample file uploaded to evidence bucket with signed URL.
- Monitoring & alerting:
  - New or changed metrics defined in the rollout dashboard.
  - SLOs for audit-log delivery latency and SIEM export success rate set.
  - Alert runbooks linked for failures in export pipeline or policy enforcement.
- Rollout & rollback plan:
  - Canary cohorts defined and toggle gating rules documented.
  - Automatic fallback policy configured (e.g., fallback to previous role mapping or disable export).
  - Manual rollback steps tested in staging.

Acceptance criteria (security reviewer must confirm):
- RBAC tests: pass and cover 90% of changed policy branches.
- Audit events: all new events contain required fields; synthetic tests show no >1% malformed events.
- SIEM exports: sample export conforms to schema and contains no unredacted PII.
- Evidence bundle: contains PR, role map, unit test output, sample logs, export sample, and monitoring dashboard snapshot.

Evidence bundle structure (what to attach to the release ticket):
- PR link and description (string).
- ROLE-MAP.md (text) with before/after rows.
- ci/rbac-policy-tests-results.txt (artifact).
- audit-samples/launch-YYYYMMDD.log (10–20 examples).
- siem-exports/sample-payload.json (masked).
- dashboards/launch-<id>.png (metric snapshots).
- export-throughput-report.pdf (load test).

Automated evidence collection points (recommended CI jobs):
- rbac-policy-unit-tests: runs on PR and on main; uploads results to artifacts and notifies security-bot.
- audit-schema-linter: lints new event definitions against canonical schema (fails PR).
- siem-export-smoke: spins up a short-lived pipeline in staging and uploads sample export.

Exception approval flow (for items that cannot be met before launch):
1) Owner opens SEC-EXCEPTION ticket and populates the Exception Request template in the ticket body (fields: requirement, rationale, compensating controls, mitigation timeline).
2) Triage: Security reviewer assigns risk level (Low/Medium/High) and records temporary compensating controls (e.g., increased monitoring, manual review).
3) If Medium or High risk, schedule a 30-min exception review call including product, eng lead, SRE, and legal.
4) Approval options: Approve (with deadline), Approve with additional mitigation, Deny. Approvals must be recorded with explicit sign-off (name, role, timestamp).
5) Exceptions are time-boxed; reopen SEC-EXCEPTION if not remediated by the deadline.

Sign-off matrix (who must sign):
- Product owner: confirms business justification and rollout plan.
- Engineering lead: confirms tests, rollback, and toggle readiness.
- Security reviewer: confirms RBAC, audit, and SIEM compliance.
- SRE: confirms monitoring, alerting, and rollback.
- Legal/Compliance (for exports or PII): signs for data protections.

Template sign-off statement (copy into release ticket):
"I, <name>, in my role as <role>, have reviewed the evidence bundle for <release id>. I confirm that I accept the security acceptance criteria described in the runbook (or I have approved a documented exception)."

Post-launch verification (0–72 hrs):
- 0–4 hrs: confirm audit ingestion rate and no malformed events >0.5% in production samplings.
- 4–24 hrs: verify SIEM exports appear in downstream systems and no PII incidents flagged.
- 24–72 hrs: review retrospective for anomalies and close release ticket if no findings.

Audit trail & retention:
- All evidence bundles preserved in the security-evidence bucket for 2 years.
- Audit log schema versions recorded in the schema registry (schema id + git commit).
- SIEM export mapping versions pinned alongside release.

Operational playbook snippets (quick commands):
- Collect last 100 audit events for unit X: kubectl logs -n audit deployment/audit-forwarder --tail=100 | grep "unitX" > audit-samples.txt
- Re-run siem export smoke in staging: ./infra/ci/run_siem_smoke.sh --env=staging --release <id>

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Missing fields in audit event -> run audit-schema-linter locally against event definitions; add defaulted fields and re-run unit tests.
- Cardinality spike -> add sampling or drop non-essential high-cardinality fields; consult SRE for retention cadence.
- Export pipeline backpressure -> increase batch window or enable throttling for non-critical exports.

Open questions (owner must resolve before final sign-off):
- Do we need explicit consent flows documented for user_identifiers emitted to SIEM for this feature?
- Is there a retention exception request needed for extended audit storage?

Appendix: quick checklist for reviewers (copy/paste into review comment)
- [ ] Roles updated and justified
- [ ] RBAC unit tests present and passing
- [ ] Audit events mapped and sample logs attached
- [ ] SIEM export sample conforms to redaction rules
- [ ] Monitoring & rollback verified
- [ ] Evidence bundle uploaded to security-evidence

Document maintenance notes:
- Owner: Security Engineering (Aisha Patel).
- Review cadence: every major RBAC release or annually.
- Where to edit: CONFLUENCE -> Security -> Launch Runbooks.
